title: Onboard a VCF Operations notification plugin and rule, and report a partially applied change accurately
prompt:
Implement the two exported functions in `module/VcfOpsNotificationOnboarding/VcfOpsNotificationOnboarding.psm1` so the module onboards an outbound notification target in VMware Cloud Foundation Operations 9.1. Edit only that file.

The protected `docs/contract.json` is a focused projection derived directly from `specifications/vcf-operations/vcf-operations-openapi.json` in VMware's Apache-2.0 `vmware/vcf-api-specs` repository at immutable VCF 9.1 release commit `c3f3b52c845dd967cabbc21680e893292077d5ba`. `docs/official_sources.json` records that commit, the exact specification path, and every operationId in the projection. No rendered documentation page is a contract source. This is the VCF Operations API itself, served under the `/suite-api` base path; the sibling `log-management-openapi.json` is a different API and is not involved. Use only these specification operationIds: `acquireToken`, `getCurrentVersionOfServer`, `getAlertPluginTypes`, `createAlertPlugin`, `getNotificationTemplates`, and `createNotificationPluginRule`.

Drive every request through the `VMware.Sdk.Vcf.Ops` PowerCLI cmdlets, which the environment installs as a prerequisite. Do not vendor them, do not add dependencies, and do not hand-roll HTTP with `Invoke-RestMethod`, `Invoke-WebRequest`, or `HttpClient`. `Connect-VcfOpsServer` performs `acquireToken` and `getCurrentVersionOfServer`; each remaining operation has an `Invoke-VcfOps<OperationId>` cmdlet, and request models are built with the matching `Initialize-VcfOps<schema>` cmdlet.

Preserve the supplied function names, parameters, and parameter types. `Connect-VcfOpsNotificationSession` opens the session and returns the connection; `-AuthSource` is optional in the `username-password` schema and must only be sent when the caller supplies it. `New-VcfOpsNotificationBinding` applies the change against that connection.

`New-VcfOpsNotificationBinding` performs four ordered steps, named `VerifyPluginType` (`getAlertPluginTypes`), `CreatePlugin` (`createAlertPlugin`), `ResolveTemplate` (`getNotificationTemplates`), and `CreateRule` (`createNotificationPluginRule`). `VerifyPluginType` confirms `-PluginTypeId` appears in the server's supported list before anything is created. `CreatePlugin` creates the plugin instance from `-PluginName`, `-PluginTypeId`, one `name`/`value` pair per `-ConfigValue` entry in the order supplied, and `-PluginDescription`. `ResolveTemplate` runs only when `-TemplateName` is supplied: it filters server-side on the `name` query parameter and requires exactly one match. `CreateRule` creates the rule from `-RuleName`, the `pluginId` the server assigned, the resolved `templateId`, `-CollectorGroupId`, and `-Criticality`.

The change is not transactional and the projection names no delete or update operation, so a step that fails leaves everything the earlier steps already changed in place. Never attempt a rollback or any cleanup call. Instead, return a report object even when the change fails, and never throw for a status the specification declares. The report carries `Succeeded`, `PluginTypeSupported`, `PluginId`, `TemplateId`, `RuleId`, `OrphanedPluginId`, `FailedOperationId`, `FailureStatusCode`, `FailureMessage`, and `Steps`. `Steps` holds one entry per step, in order, each with `Name`, `OperationId`, and an `Outcome` of `Succeeded`, `Failed`, `Skipped`, or `NotAttempted`. `Skipped` means the step was deliberately not needed; `NotAttempted` means an earlier failure stopped the run before it. A step whose `Outcome` is `Skipped` or `NotAttempted` must issue no request at all. `OrphanedPluginId` is the created `pluginId` when a plugin was created but the binding did not complete, and null otherwise. When a request fails, report the declared HTTP status in `FailureStatusCode` and the server's own message in `FailureMessage`; a non-success status surfaces as a terminating error whose `InnerException` is a `VMware.Binding.OpenApi.Client.ApiException` carrying `ErrorCode` and `ErrorContent`. When a step fails without an HTTP failure, such as an unsupported plugin type on a request that returned 200, leave `FailureStatusCode` null rather than inventing a status.

Send exactly what the caller supplied. In `notification-plugin`, only `name` and `pluginTypeId` are required; `enabled` is documented read-only and `pluginId` is update-only, so neither belongs in a create. In `notification-rule`, only `name` and `pluginId` are required; `enabled` and `sendHeartbeat` carry server-side defaults and `id` is assigned on create. Every `getNotificationTemplates` query parameter is optional and `page` and `pageSize` have server-side defaults. Omit every unset optional field completely rather than transmitting it as an empty string, `null`, `false`, a zero, or an empty collection, and emit no bare `?` on a request that carries no query parameters. Preserve values the caller did supply.

Verification runs the module against a loopback mock of the contract and asserts the exact wire shape of every recorded request; no live VMware endpoint is contacted.

prerequisites.dependency_source: PowerShell Gallery, installed by the environment before the task starts

scenario: Onboarding an outbound notification target verifies the plugin type, creates the plugin instance, resolves a payload template and finally creates the notification rule; the rule is rejected with a declared 422 after the plugin already exists, so the run must report the created pluginId as orphaned instead of claiming success or pretending the change was undone, and a first-step rejection must leave every later step reported as NotAttempted with nothing created.
constraint: The contract-pinned loopback request log proves the exact create and query wire shape, including that unset optional fields such as description, templateId and collectorGroupId are omitted entirely rather than sent as empty strings, that read-only and defaulted fields such as enabled and sendHeartbeat are never transmitted, that a skipped or unattempted step issues no request, and that no rollback or off-contract operation is ever called.
